name: cpp-terminal
listed_description: Small header only C++ library for writing multiplatform terminal applications.
reason: README (opened) says it is 'a small and simple replacement for ncurses' and lists ncurses and termbox as inspirations, but gives no benchmark numbers; the repo has no benchmark directory (cmake, cpp-terminal, docs, examples, tests only). Claim is about size and portability, not speed.

name: EasyLogger
listed_description: An ultra-lightweight, high-performance C/C++ log library.
reason: README (opened) states footprint only (ROM<1.6K, RAM<0.3K) and a qualitative comparison to log4c and zlog (fewer features), with no timing or throughput numbers against any baseline. A WebSearch for EasyLogger benchmarks found MuggleWei/cc_log_benchmark, whose README (opened) lists nine libraries and does not include EasyLogger. Directional claim only.

name: FINAL CUT
listed_description: A terminal user interface, a modern replacement for Ncurses.
reason: doc/benchmark.md (opened) has a Rotozoomer table of FINAL CUT frame rates across 15 terminal emulators and consoles (for example XTerm 116.598 fps, GNOME-Terminal 117.033 fps at 80x24 on an old PC), measuring terminal output speed, not FINAL CUT against ncurses or termbox. No numeric baseline comparison anywhere in the README or docs.

name: Kitsune
listed_description: Efficient, general-purpose framework for dynamic software updating.
reason: kitsune-dsu.com, www.cs.umd.edu and the OOPSLA paper hosts are EGRESS_BLOCKED here, and no GitHub repo was found (github.com/kitsune-dsu/kitsune is 404). Web search snippets only say the OOPSLA 2012 paper (Hayden et al.) reports 'essentially no performance overhead' and fast update times for Redis, Memcached and others; no figures and no speed-versus-restart baseline were obtainable. Its efficiency claim is low overhead relative to the unmodified program, not a speedup over a faster baseline. Retry where the UMD paper or the project site is reachable (journal version: hayden14kitsune-journal).

name: Libclsph
listed_description: An OpenCL based GPU accelerated SPH fluid simulation library.
reason: README (opened) says it was made 'to explore the possibility of using OpenCL to speed up' SPH simulation and links two demo videos, with no numbers. Wiki home (opened) lists a 'Getting the best performance' page whose content failed to load; no CPU or other-library baseline numbers found. Directional claim only.

name: liblfds
listed_description: Portable lock-free data structure library. Public domain (more exactly, whatever license you want).
reason: Benchmark results exist (libbenchmark compares liblfds against locking versions of the same structures; blog posts liblfds.org/slblog/2016-02 to 2016-05, and a btree benchmark said to show lock-free winning by 5x to 10x) but liblfds.org and www.liblfds.org are EGRESS_BLOCKED, and the github.com/liblfds mirrors (liblfds, liblfds7.1.1; README says development moved to liblfds.org self-hosted git) hold no benchmark results. Only WebSearch summaries were seen, which also say pthread mutex won one queue benchmark and pthread spinlock won at maximum thread count, so the claim is mixed; no named baseline, hardware or flags could be verified. Retry where liblfds.org is reachable (release 7.1.1 libbenchmark results).
